1.91.59.en: Adam tore the covenant of purity and obedience to the Giver of goodness.

1.91.60.en: In Adam we became branches in the wild olive tree, and by faith we became the offspring of Abraham spiritually, grafted into the fruitful olive tree through the work of the Holy Spirit.

1.91.61.en: v Through Isaac, the son of the promise, we realized our sonship to God.

1.91.62.en: Isaac filled the heart of his father with gladness and joy.

1.91.63.en: And we, by the Holy Spirit of God, have become the object of the Father's delight.

1.91.64.en: v Isaac, the son of obedience, begot Jacob, the father of all the tribes.

1.91.65.en: For my sake You came, O my Savior, not to belong to a certain tribe, nor to inherit a portion in the Promised Land.

1.91.66.en: But to give me Yourself as a portion for my soul, that I may rejoice in You eternally.

1.91.67.en: You are my all, O desire of my heart!

2.0.0.en: These are the sons of Israel;

2.0.1.en: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, [1]

2.1.0.en: Dan, Joseph, and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. [2]

2.1.1.en: He begins with the names of the sons of Jacob, whom God called Israel, but they are not in the order of the date of birth.

2.1.2.en: The sons of Jacob and the twelve tribes occur more than 20 times in the Holy Bible, each time in a different order according to the purpose of mentioning the tribes. They occur in the First Book of Chronicles three times (1 Chr 2:1-2; 2:3-8:34; 12:23-27). I would like to write a special appendix on the order of the names of these tribes in the most important places in the Holy Bible.

2.1.3.en: The book does not refer here to any event in the life of Jacob; what concerns it is to record his name as God gave it to him, "Israel," since this name points to the attachment of the twelve tribes to him.

2.1.4.en: In the midst of distress Jacob laid his head on a stone, and lay down on the way, to see the heavens open, and a heavenly ladder set up on the earth with its top touching heaven (Gen 28:12-15). In this place Jacob received a divine promise for himself and his offspring: "In thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed... for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of" (Gen 28:14-15). What is the secret of the blessing that is in him and in his offspring, except that in his loins was Judah, who begets David, and from his offspring the Word of God becomes incarnate, who blesses all the families of the earth by His Cross and the power of His resurrection?!

2.1.5.en: v The stone under his head is Christ, for he had had no stone under his head before, but he had one at that time when he fled from his persecutor. When he was in his father's house, at rest according to the flesh, he did not enjoy a stone under his head. He left his house like a poor man and became like one alone, having nothing but a staff, and in the same night he found a stone to put under his head. And when he had a pillow of this kind, his head rested through the vision he saw[1].

2.1.6.en: St. Jerome He spoke afterward about the line of the twelve tribes in the following chapters, and it seems that the writer hastens as fast as possible to the emergence of the kingdom of David, which occupies the two books, where he wishes to speak of the house of David seated on the throne, in order to carry our thought across to the Son of David, the King of kings.

2.1.7.en: It is observed in the mention of the sons of Jacob (Israel) that they are not mentioned in order, but he began with the sons of Leah, then the two sons of Rachel (Joseph and Benjamin) between Dan and Naphtali the sons of Bilhah, and at the end the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, Gad and Asher.

2.1.8.en: We observe in the genealogies that he paid attention to the genealogies of the two tribes of Judah and Levi, the royal tribe and the priestly tribe. The genealogies of Judah occupy 102 verses, Levi 81 verses, while the genealogies of all the rest of the tribes together occupy 126 verses.

2.1.9.en: He wanted to affirm the obligation of cooperation among the tribes in spite of the differences between them, each tribe completing the rest of the tribes and needing them, and they needing it and not able to do without it, especially between the royal tribe and the priestly tribe.

2.1.10.en: We will see this in a practical and clear way when all the tribes meet together in Hebron around David to make him king over them all. Each tribe offers what it has of abilities and gifts, not in a spirit of competition or jealousy or boasting or superiority, but as it is said: "All these men of war, that could keep rank, came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel... of one heart... for there was joy in Israel" (1 Chr 12:38-40).

2.1.11.en: I mention, by way of example, what some of the tribes were distinguished by:

2.1.12.en: a. The tribe of Judah, the foremost and royal.

2.1.13.en: b. The tribe of Levi, indispensable, from which came the priests the sons of Kohath, and the Levites with their varied roles in service, guarding and praise.

2.1.14.en: c. The tribe of Benjamin, who accompanied Judah wherever they were found, and who were ahead of others in choosing David as king, although they were brothers of Saul, who resisted and envied David.

2.1.15.en: d. Joseph, the one with two portions, the only one who became two tribes: Ephraim and Manasseh.

2.1.16.en: We will return, God willing, to speak about all the tribes, especially Judah and Levi. But here we wish to affirm that the sons of Jacob or Israel... found in David the king a leader who gathers all together to work for the glory of God!

2.1.17.en: The sons of Jacob or Israel bear types, especially Joseph, who was greatly beloved of his father. I content myself here with quoting a little of what the Fathers said about him as a type of the Lord Christ:

2.1.18.en: v Jacob loved his son, because the Father loves His only-begotten Son, for He says: "This is my beloved Son" (Mt 3:17)[2].

2.1.19.en: Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles v Joseph was persecuted, and his brothers were the persecutors. Joseph was glorified, and his persecutors bowed down to him, and his dreams and visions were fulfilled.

2.1.20.en: The persecuted Joseph was a type of the persecuted Jesus.

2.1.21.en: His father clothed Joseph with a coat of many colors, and Jesus His Father clothed with a body from the Virgin.

2.1.22.en: His father loved Joseph more than his brothers, and Jesus is the dear beloved of His Father.

2.1.23.en: Joseph saw visions and dreamed dreams, and the visions and the prophets were fulfilled in Jesus.

2.1.24.en: Joseph was a shepherd with his brothers, and Jesus is the Chief Shepherd.

2.1.25.en: When his father sent him to visit his brothers, they saw Joseph coming and planned to kill him, and when the Father sent Jesus to visit His brothers, they said: "This is the heir; come, let us kill him" (Mt 21:38).

2.1.26.en: The brothers of Joseph cast their brother into the pit, and Jesus was brought down by His brothers to dwell among the dead.

2.1.27.en: Joseph came up from the pit, and Jesus rose from the dead.

2.1.28.en: Joseph, after he rose from the pit, had authority over his brothers, and Jesus, after He dwelt among the dead, His Father gave Him a great and glorified name (Phil 2:9) that His brothers might serve Him and His enemies be subdued under His feet.

2.1.29.en: After Joseph's brothers knew him, they were ashamed and afraid and astonished before his greatness, and when Jesus comes at the end of time and declares His greatness, His brothers will be ashamed and afraid and tremble before Him because they crucified Him.

2.1.30.en: Moreover, Joseph was sold into Egypt on the counsel of Judah, and Jesus was delivered to the Jews by the hands of Judas Iscariot.

2.1.31.en: When they sold Joseph, his brothers did not answer a word, and Jesus also did not speak nor answer the judges who tried Him.

2.1.32.en: Joseph was delivered to prison unjustly by his master, and Jesus was condemned unjustly by the sons of His people.

2.1.33.en: Joseph surrendered his two garments, one in the hands of his brothers and the other in the hand of his master's wife, and Jesus surrendered His garments, and they were divided among the soldiers.

2.1.34.en: Joseph, when he was thirty years old, stood before Pharaoh and became lord of Egypt, and Jesus, when He reached thirty, came to the Jordan to be baptized, and received the Spirit and went out preaching.

2.1.35.en: Joseph sustained Egypt with bread, and Jesus sustained the whole world with the bread of life.

2.1.36.en: Joseph took the daughter of the wicked, unclean priest as his wife, and Jesus betrothed to Himself the Church from the unclean Gentiles.

2.1.37.en: Joseph died and was buried in Egypt, and Jesus died and was buried in Jerusalem.

2.2.0.en: The bones of Joseph were brought up by his brothers from Egypt, and Jesus His Father raised from the dwelling of death and He put on His body, and was lifted up with it to heaven without corruption[3].

2.3.0.en: 3 The sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah: which three were born unto him of the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess. And Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the LORD; and he slew him. 4 And Tamar his daughter in law bare him Pharez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah were five. 5 The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. 6 And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara: five of them in all. 7 And the sons of Carmi; Achar, the troubler of Israel, who transgressed in the thing accursed. 8 And the sons of Ethan; Azariah. 9 The sons also of Hezron, that were born unto him; Jerahmeel, and Ram, and Chelubai. 10 And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah; 11 And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, 12 And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse, 13 And Jesse begat his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimma the third, 14 Nethaneel the fourth, Raddai the fifth, 15 Ozem the sixth, David the seventh: 16 Whose sisters were Zeruiah, and Abigail. And the sons of Zeruiah; Abishai, and Joab, and Asahel, three. 17 And Abigail bare Amasa: and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmeelite.

2.3.1.en: The sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah:

2.3.2.en: which three were born unto him of the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess.

2.3.3.en: And Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the LORD; and he slew him. [3]

2.3.4.en: The First Book of Chronicles centers on the tribe of Judah, although Judah is the fourth son of Jacob, to hasten the believer to the meeting with David the prophet, and to become acquainted in Second Chronicles with the house of David, especially the kings, whether Solomon before the division or his son Rehoboam and all the kings of Judah after the division until the fall under the Babylonian captivity and the return to Jerusalem. The purpose of these two books is the entry of every soul into the enjoyment of the Son of David, the Word incarnate, who establishes His kingdom in the heart of the true believer.

2.3.5.en: Judah was the foremost of his brothers, because from him the Messiah comes, for his father blessed him, saying: "The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be" (Gen 49:10).

2.3.6.en: With all this the writer reveals Judah, who held the position of the birthright, so that his tribe became the royal tribe leading Israel; the Holy Bible mentioned the weaknesses of Judah, among them the following:

2.3.7.en: a. He married a Canaanite girl, "the daughter of Shua" (Gen 38:1-3). The Holy Bible did not hide this fact, but repeated it in (1 Chr 2:3), to affirm that the choice of Judah as the royal tribe from whose offspring the Word of God becomes incarnate does not rest on human righteousness or personal merit, but on the wondrous grace of God, who turned this wrong conduct to good. For by his marriage to the Canaanite woman he opened the door of hope before the Gentiles, declaring that salvation is offered to all, to the Jew as to the Gentile.

2.3.8.en: The daughter of Shua: the word "Shua" is a Semitic name meaning "wealth," and he was a Canaanite man. Perhaps Judah married her for the wealth of her father or for her beauty. But God by His grace granted that there should become incarnate from his offspring the Creator of heaven and earth, the source of true wealth and beauty.

2.3.9.en: b. The daughter of Shua bore Judah his three sons: Er, Onan and Shelah. It is said of his firstborn son: "And Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the LORD; and he slew him." Er is a Hebrew name meaning "watchful." Neither the Book of Genesis nor the First Book of Chronicles says what Er's sin was, but is content to say that God allowed his early death, because he was wicked in the sight of the Lord. Most likely God allowed him to be killed in Canaan at an early age because of the multitude of his evils. This is the firstborn of Judah by the Canaanite woman!

2.3.10.en: History has covered over the evil of Er, but since Er persisted in it and offered no repentance for it, it remained engraved, to be declared on the great day of the Lord. So it befits us not to be concerned to cover up our evils, but to wash them in the blood of the Lamb through sincere repentance, and the return to the bosom of God, open to every person however great his evil.

2.3.11.en: c. When Er died without having a son, his brother Onan married Tamar, his brother's widow, to beget a son who would be attributed to his dead brother, and Onan died without begetting. Judah feared for his third son Shelah, lest he marry her and die (Gen 38:6-11). Tamar resorted to a ruse to bear a son: she took off her widow's garments, and covered herself with a veil and disguised herself, and Judah thought her a harlot, and asked to come in to her. And when she conceived he ordered her to be burned, but she disclosed to him that the one in her womb was from him. Judah went in to her, supposing her a harlot, and was not ashamed to ask about the harlot among many, and when he discovered that Tamar was with child he asked for her to be burned! This Judah confessed that Tamar, the wife of his wicked son Er, was more righteous than he.

2.3.12.en: This is Judah, whose tribe later became the royal tribe. The Lord's choice to become man from this tribe, with Judah at its head, and to have in His lineage Tamar, the widow of wicked Er, confirms to us that He came for the sake of sinners and all the nations, opening the gates of heaven before every person who clings to Him, whatever his past or lineage or nationality. He is a lover of all mankind.

2.3.13.en: Although Reuben is the firstborn son of Jacob, the line of genealogies here began with Judah, though he is the fourth of the sons of Jacob, because the tribe of Judah was distinguished as the royal tribe, and the Lord Christ, the Word incarnate, came from his offspring (Gen 38:2-10, 13-30). From it came David the king, and from it St. Mary, in whose womb the King of kings became incarnate.

2.3.14.en: Although the tribe of Judah took the place of precedence, yet the Lord put to death Judah's firstborn "Er," because he was wicked in the sight of the Lord.

2.3.15.en: The hideous sin of Reuben, for which the Scripture does not say he offered repentance, cost him much: 1. The loss of his privileges as firstborn. 2. The loss of the possibility that the Messiah would come from his offspring. 3. The loss of his life.

2.3.16.en: His name became a stigma of shame in the record of his clan. The psalmist says: "For evildoers shall be cut off: but those that wait upon the LORD, they shall inherit the earth" (Ps 37:9).

2.3.17.en: v These (the wicked), according to the testimony of the psalmist, have tongues like a sharp sword, and teeth that are spears and arrows (Ps 57:4). But the wonderful thing is that while they attack others they do not harm them, but they themselves are torn by their own tongues, because they carry within them anger, resentment, envy, deceit, hatred and bitterness...

2.4.0.en: And although they are unable to harm others, it turns back upon themselves first and against them, as the psalmist prays, saying: "Their sword shall enter into their own heart" (Ps 37:15). And there is also said of such a one, "His own iniquities shall take the wicked himself, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sins" (Prov 5:22)[4].

2.4.1.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic A question remains for us: why did God choose the tribe of Judah to be the royal tribe in spite of the faults mentioned before?

2.4.2.en: It seems to me that David, who was of the offspring of Judah, was chosen so that the incarnate Word of God might come from his offspring, for the following reasons: 1. Because of the purity of his heart, for God Himself testified of him that he was a man after God's own heart (Acts 13:22). 2. Because he rose to the commandment of the New Testament while still under the shadow of the Law, for he loved Saul, who bore bitter enmity toward him and tried with all his powers and means to kill him. 3. He was not concerned to take the throne in spite of God's promise of it to him when he was still a little boy, but what concerned him was the heavenly Kingdom. 4. He was the first man of praise even in the midst of his afflictions. 5. Because in many situations he was a type of the Lord Christ, as we shall see in the appendix to chapter ten. 6. With every fall into sin he would flood his bed every night with his tears. 7. He devoted his zeal and energies to preparing materials and arrangements for building the house of the Lord, in spite of the Lord's refusal of his request to build it, and His granting that his son should undertake this task.

2.4.3.en: So for the sake of David, who was in the loins of his grandfather Judah, this tribe was chosen to have this privilege. If the tribe of Judah had its faults, and David himself also, this did not deprive David of God's own testimony about him. Therefore we should not wonder that the Lord Christ is called the Son of David, despite his faults, and this has become His title to this day, and the Lord did not bear the title Son of Judah or Son of Abraham.

2.4.4.en: How wonderful is the love of God, for the blessing of David's purity of heart and the tears of his sincere repentance had their effect upon his ancestors up to Judah the son of Jacob and his tribe, and extended to his descendants, as we shall see in our study of Second Chronicles!

2.4.5.en: v Some are astonished that Matthew saw fit to mention in the genealogy of the Lord Christ the name of "Tamar," who seems like a harlot, and of Ruth, and of her who had been Uriah's and whom David married after he killed her husband, and did not mention the names of the holy women such as Sarah, Rebekah and Rachel...

2.4.6.en: For since Matthew was proclaiming the Lord born in the flesh, who was made sin for all, and who was exposed to insults and crucifixion, he believed that it was not fitting to show Him defending Himself against insult by having sinners among His ancestors...

2.4.7.en: So also the Church is not ashamed to be chosen from among sinners!

2.4.8.en: St. Ambrose Onan: the second son of Judah (1 Chr 2:3).

2.4.9.en: Shelah: a Hebrew name meaning "petition," the third of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 2:3).

2.5.0.en: And Tamar his daughter in law bare him Pharez and Zerah.

2.5.1.en: All the sons of Judah were five. [4]

2.6.0.en: Tamar[5]: we spoke of her before in the commentary on the preceding verse, and we saw that, since she desired, like every Hebrew woman, to bear a son, even if from her father-in-law, because she desired that the Messiah the Savior should come from her offspring, God fulfilled her request.

2.6.1.en: She agreed to expose her life to danger, so she took off her widow's garments, and put a veil on her face, and was not ashamed to appear as a harlot, not for the lust of the flesh but for the sake of bearing a child. For she clung to her father-in-law, who was a man advanced in years... And her purity is shown in that, when she disclosed the matter, she did not ask after that to marry her husband's brother, but lived with her father-in-law, and it is said: "And he knew her again no more" (Gen 38:26).

2.6.2.en: For her faith's sake she desired to bear, while Judah in his old age committed adultery... Therefore he says: "She hath been more righteous than I" (Gen 38:26). And Tamar became a living example that prevents us from condemning, however clear and tangible the signs of sin appear. St. Ambrose commented much on this phrase "she hath been more righteous than I" in his discourse on repentance, asking every person, even the bishop, not to condemn anyone, but to show mercy and compassion to sinners; among his words:

2.6.3.en: v O Lord, grant me to have the falls of every person before me, that I may bear them with him, and not rebuke him in pride, but grieve and weep, for in my weeping for others I weep for myself, saying: "She hath been more righteous than I."

2.6.4.en: Suppose a girl has fallen, deceived and swept away by circumstances that provoke sin; well! We who are older may fall also! In us also the law of the flesh wars against the law of our minds, and makes us captives to sin, so that we do what we do not want (Rom 7:23). Her youth may be an excuse for her, but what is my excuse?! She must learn, but I must know that "she hath been more righteous than I"...

2.7.0.en: May we then not be ashamed to confess that our fault is more hideous than the fault of one whom we think deserving of rebuke, for this is what Judah did, who reproved Tamar, and when he remembered his sin said: "She hath been more righteous than I"... He accused himself before others accused him[6].

2.7.1.en: St. Ambrose By this deed of faith Tamar was made worthy to be a grandmother of the Lord Christ, her blood running in His veins, so that the Evangelist Matthew recorded her name in the genealogy of the Lord Christ (Mt 1:3), while he did not record the name of Sarah or Rebekah or other blessed mothers.

2.7.2.en: Tamar was a type of the company of the Gentiles which became a holy Church for the Lord, which was formerly fruitless like Tamar, like a forsaken widow with none to support her or help her. Her first kinsman Shelah did not marry her, but she clung to the second kinsman Judah... So the company of the Gentiles did not cling to the first kinsman, that is, the Mosaic Law, nor did it bind itself to circumcision and Judaizing, but clung to the second kinsman, that is, the true Judah, our Lord Jesus Christ, who came forth from the tribe of Judah.

2.7.3.en: And the wonder is that the conduct of Tamar, as recorded in Genesis chapter (Gen 38), bore many symbols that correspond to what the Church of the Gentiles enjoyed; we mention among them:

2.7.4.en: a. Tamar put off her widow's garments, in order to cling to Judah (Gen 38:14), and so the Gentiles put off the garments of the old man to put on the new man, who befits its union with the eternal Bridegroom, indeed the Lord Christ Himself became its new garment.

2.7.5.en: b. Tamar covered her face with a veil (Gen 38:15), and the Gentiles, having received the faith, live here as in a riddle, until they meet the Bridegroom face to face, and see Him in the fullness of His glory and the greatness of His splendor, and come to know the loftiness of His surpassing mysteries.

2.7.6.en: c. Tamar sat at the entrance of Enaim (Gen 38:14), that is, the entrance of two springs, as though she were the Church of the Gentiles, which did not enjoy the spring of the Old Testament alone but also the spring of the New Testament with it.

2.7.7.en: d. Tamar enjoyed the signet of Judah and his bracelets and his staff (Gen 38:18), that is, the seal of sonship to God and the heavenly crown together with the wood of the life-giving Cross.

2.7.8.en: e. The signs of pregnancy appeared after three months (Gen 38:24), as though she were the Church of the Gentiles which bore spiritual fruits, through its faith in the Holy Trinity (3 months) and its enjoyment of the risen life in Christ Jesus, who rose on the third day.

2.7.9.en: v (Tamar) longed to have children from her father-in-law when she saw that her mother-in-law had died... This was not for lack of purity, far from it! but to avoid remaining without a memorial. In fact, what happened was by a divine plan, and the result was that her plan was accomplished...

2.7.10.en: May whoever hears this not blame Tamar. As I said before, she was fulfilling the divine plan, so no blame is cast upon her, and Judah did not make any accusation against her.

2.7.11.en: I mean that you notice here that the genealogy of Christ bears her two sons.

2.8.0.en: For in particular the two children born to him signified the two peoples, representing the Jewish life and the spiritual life[7].

2.8.1.en: St. John Chrysostom v Tamar was afraid lest she be seized and killed in revenge for his two sons, since she was accused of being the cause of their death. She asked for a sign... She appears to him in another guise so that he would not kill her, and she offers him an invitation to lie with her from his own mouth...

2.8.2.en: While Tamar was asking this of God, Judah went out and saw her.

2.8.3.en: The prayer of Tamar made him incline, contrary to custom, and go to a harlot.

2.9.0.en: And when she saw him she put on a veil, because she was afraid. And after the word concerning a sign, as she had asked, she knew that God was pleased with what she had done. After that she uncovered her face without fear, and even asked a reward from the Lord of the reward[8].

2.10.0.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian In St. Cyril the Great's comment on this matter he said: [The purpose of the Holy Bible is not to relate the lives of saints, for that is not so at all, but rather to give us knowledge of the mystery of Christ through these facts, which make our speaking of Him true and clear[9].]

2.10.1.en: God by His grace made Tamar an ancestress of David, and therefore of Jesus Christ (Mt 1:3).

2.10.2.en: Pharez and Zerah: the Lord Christ came from the offspring of Pharez whom Tamar bore, and Pharez broke through before his brother Zerah while still in his mother's womb to take the birthright from him (Gen 38:27-30). At their birth, Zerah put out his hand and the midwife bound his hand with a scarlet thread, but he drew back his hand and Pharez came out first and Zerah after him. Some Fathers see in Zerah a type of the Jewish people, who should have been the firstborn, and who stretched out his hand and received the Law which centered on sacrifice (the scarlet blood), but through unbelief Pharez came out, representing the Gentiles, who obtained the firstfruits of the Spirit instead of Zerah (the Jews).

2.11.0.en: The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. [5]

2.11.1.en: Since the first and second sons of Judah died without begetting, and the genealogies of the third are mentioned in (1 Chr 4:21-23), he was content here with these two sons, as in (Gen 46:12; Num 26:21).

2.11.2.en: Hezron: a Hebrew name meaning "enclosure, fold." He was the firstborn son of Pharez, and the founder of a family in Judah (1 Chr 2:5).

2.11.3.en: From the list of the descendants of Judah [5-6], attention was given to Hezron, and his third son Caleb came, to whom special attention was given [18-20, 42-55]; and the second son of Hezron received the first place, because from his offspring came the family of David (1 Chr 2:10-17).

2.11.4.en: Hamul: a Hebrew name meaning "carried, pitied, spared," the youngest son of Pharez, and the founder of a family in Judah (1 Chr 2:5).

2.12.0.en: And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara:

2.12.2.en: "And the sons of Zerah; Zimri...": in (Josh 7:1) "Zabdi." And it is said of Solomon: "For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol" (1 Kgs 4:31). Some think that Zerah is their remote ancestor and not their father.

2.13.0.en: These five were called the sons of Mahol (1 Kgs 4:31), as they were referred to by their fame for wisdom, in which no one surpassed them except Solomon. And since the word מָחוֹל "mahol" is found among musical instruments (Ps 149:3; 150:4), and is also used for dancing, some think that these wise men are "the sons of music." Their wisdom is manifested in composing songs of praise[10].

2.13.1.en: Ethan and Heman: they became authors of inspired psalms (Ps 88-89). They are different from the musicians whom David appointed, "Heman and Asaph and Ethan" (1 Chr 15:19), who were of the tribe of Levi and not of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 6:33-44).

2.14.0.en: And the sons of Carmi; Achar, the troubler of Israel, who transgressed in the thing accursed. [7]

2.14.1.en: Carmi also was of the sons of Zerah.

2.14.2.en: It appears from (Josh 7:1) that Carmi is the son of Zabdi or Zimri, and Achar is Achan who troubled Israel. His name in Hebrew means "the troubler" or "disaster." The story of his transgression is told in (Josh 7). It is said: "But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel" (Josh 7:1). He hid from the spoil what he desired and was forbidden: "When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it" (Josh 7:21).

2.15.0.en: It befits us to beware lest the enemy creep in upon us through small things. St. Mark the Ascetic says: [Satan presents to us small sins that seem trivial in our eyes, because without this he cannot lead us to the great sins[11].]

2.16.0.en: Achan sinned, and the wrath of the Lord fell upon all the people. Origen says, commenting on the wedge of stolen gold: [It befits us not to neglect this phrase, for when one person commits a sin, wrath is brought upon the whole people. How does this disaster happen? When the priests, the leaders of the people, wish to appear lenient with sinners, because they fear their tongue, lest it rise against them, forgetting the firmness that befits their priesthood. By this they refuse to carry out what is written: "Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear" (1 Tim 5:20), and also: "Put away from among yourselves that wicked person" (1 Cor 5:13). These priests are not inflamed with zeal for the Lord, nor do they imitate the Apostle who commands: "to deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved" (1 Cor 5:5). They behave with indifference toward the counsels of the Gospel concerning sinners. When we see a sinner, let us go to him alone, then speak to him in the mouth of two or three witnesses, but if he is careless even after the Church's rebuke of him and does not repent, let him be separated from the Church and be counted as a heathen man and a publican (Mt 18:17)[12].]

2.17.0.en: v Great is the punishment that befell them (because of Achan), but a greater punishment will befall us if we do not come to our senses by looking at their fate[13].

2.18.0.en: And the sons of Ethan; Azariah. [8]

2.18.1.en: Azariah: a Hebrew name meaning "whom Jehovah has helped." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Ethan, of the sons of Zerah of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 2:8). 2. The son of Jehu the son of Obed of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:38-39).

2.19.0.en: The sons also of Hezron, that were born unto him; Jerahmeel, and Ram, and Chelubai. [9]

2.19.1.en: What is mentioned in verses [8-10] here is quoted from (Ruth 4:19-22).

2.19.2.en: Jerahmeel: a Hebrew name meaning "God has mercy," the son of Hezron the son of Pharez the son of Judah (1 Chr 2:4-9, 25-26, 33, 42).

2.19.3.en: Ram: a Hebrew name meaning "exalted, lofty." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A man of the offspring of Judah and of the sons of Hezron (1 Chr 2:9-10). 2. A man of the offspring of Judah and of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:25, 27).

2.19.4.en: Chelubai: the son of Hezron, and he is Caleb (1 Chr 2:9, 18, 42).

2.20.0.en: And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah; [10]

2.20.1.en: This list is certainly incomplete, for between Ram the son of Hezron and Nahshon the son of Amminadab there are three generations. For Nahshon the son of Amminadab was head of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness in the days of the prophet Moses (Ex 6:23; Num 1:7; 2:3), and his son Salmon married Rahab the harlot after the fall of Jericho (Mt 1:5).

2.21.0.en: And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, [11]

2.21.1.en: Also three other generations are omitted before reaching Boaz, the husband of Ruth, the grandfather of Jesse the father of David.

2.21.3.en: Boaz: he was marked by simplicity with wisdom, when he discovered the truth about Ruth the Moabitess, the poor widow of a foreign race, and her clinging to the living God, and her faithfulness to her mother-in-law. He took positive practical steps. Since he embraced Ruth although she was a Moabitess, he was made worthy that there should come from their offspring David the king and Jesus (Christ) the Son of David, the Savior of the world (see the Book of Ruth).

2.22.0.en: And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse, [12]

2.22.1.en: Obed: a Hebrew name meaning "servant." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Ruth and Boaz, who is the father of Jesse the father of David (1 Chr 2:12). In the genealogies of Judah special attention was given to the father of David, Jesse [10-12], and after that his sons [13-15]. 2. The son of Ephlal, of the offspring of Sheshan, of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 2:37).

2.22.2.en: Jesse: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "man," the son of Obed and father of David and grandson of Ruth and Boaz, and the father of seven sons who had offspring (1 Chr 2:15), and an eighth who died without having offspring, and he had two daughters by a wife other than David's mother (1 Chr 2:16).

2.23.0.en: And Jesse begat his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimma the third, [13]

2.23.1.en: Eliab: a Hebrew name meaning "God is Father."

2.23.2.en: Abinadab: a Hebrew name meaning "the Father is generous or willing."

2.23.3.en: Shimea: (with a fatha on the ayin) a Hebrew name meaning "God hears," and (with a kasra on the ayin) a Hebrew name meaning "Jehovah, let him hear."

2.24.0.en: Nethaneel the fourth, Raddai the fifth, [14]

2.24.1.en: Nethaneel: a Hebrew name meaning "God has given," the fourth son of Jesse, that is, the brother of David (1 Chr 2:12-14).

2.24.2.en: Raddai: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "Jehovah has subdued," a brother of David, the fifth of the sons of Jesse (1 Chr 2:14).

2.25.0.en: Ozem the sixth, David the seventh: [15]

2.25.1.en: Ozem: a Hebrew name, probably meaning "angry." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A son of Jesse and brother of David of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:15). 2. A son of Jerahmeel in the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:25).

2.25.2.en: David: although he was the youngest of the sons of Jesse, he was chosen by God to begin the royal line through the generations until it reached its peak with the coming of the Son of David. He is perhaps one of the most famous figures of the Old Testament; the men of faith were looking for the coming of the Messiah, the Son of David. David the king and prophet is a wonderful example of purity of heart and holy love, and humility with courage, and his love of praise, and reliance on God, and his zeal for the glory of God, and his love and devotion to the people of God, and his longing to build the Temple. He had his bitter falls, but with every fall he rose in a spirit of sincere repentance in complete submission to the Lord's disciplines of him. This raised him in the eyes of God, so Jesus (Christ) came from his offspring, and he became a great example of repentance (Acts 13:22; 1 Kgs 16 ff.; 1 Chr 19 ff.).

2.25.3.en: In First Samuel it is mentioned that Jesse had eight sons (1 Sam 16:6-11), but here only seven are mentioned, because the eighth died without marrying or married and did not beget a child, and therefore he is no longer counted in the genealogies, and his name is not known.

2.26.0.en: Whose sisters were Zeruiah, and Abigail.

2.26.1.en: And the sons of Zeruiah; Abishai, and Joab, and Asahel, three. [16]

2.26.2.en: Zeruiah and Abigail: the line of genealogies cared not only for David the king but even for his two sisters.

2.26.3.en: Zeruiah is a Hebrew name, most probably meaning "perfumed with balm"; and Abigail is a Hebrew name meaning "my father is joy." They are two sisters, the daughters of Nahash (2 Sam 17:25), which is another name of Jesse, or the name of the wife of Jesse, or after the death of Nahash Jesse took his widow and she bore him David and his brothers, so Zeruiah and Abigail were their sisters by their mother and not by their father.

2.26.4.en: Abishai or Abshai: he and his two brothers Joab and Asahel were among the prominent heroes of their uncle David. He was brave, very impetuous. He saved David's life, and killed three hundred men at one time with his spear (see 2 Sam 23:18-23). He advised his uncle to kill King Saul while he slept at night, but he said to him: "Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the LORD'S anointed, and be guiltless?" (1 Sam 26:9). He was marked by his faithfulness and devotion to David. He accompanied him in his wars from the face of Absalom.

2.26.5.en: When Shimei the son of Gera of the house of Saul cursed, Abishai wanted to kill him immediately, but David forbade him (2 Sam 16:5-14).

2.26.6.en: Joab: a Hebrew name meaning "Jehovah is Father," the firstborn of the sons of Zeruiah, David's sister, and the commander of his army. He was a skilled strategist and a brave warrior, who helped in reconciling David with his son Absalom. But he was a stubborn avenger, who carried out David's plan to kill Uriah the Hittite, and also killed Absalom in spite of David's orders not to kill him, and conspired with Adonijah against David and Solomon. He avenged the killing of his brother, and killed Abner.

2.26.7.en: Asahel: a Hebrew name meaning "God has made," the son of Zeruiah (David's sister) and brother of Joab and Abishai. He was famous for speed, for he was light of foot like a wild gazelle. He was one of the heroes in David's army. He took part in the battle of Gibeon, where he pursued his enemy Abner and wanted to kill him, but it was Abner who killed him, and that was before David took the kingship (1 Chr 2:16).

2.27.0.en: And Abigail bare Amasa: and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmeelite. [17]

2.27.1.en: Amasa: a Hebrew name, a shortening of the name Amasai, the son of Jether the Ishmaelite and Abigail the sister of David and the cousin of Joab (1 Chr 2:17).

2.27.2.en: Jether the Ishmaelite[14]: Jether is a Hebrew name meaning "excellence." In (2 Sam 17:25) he is "Ithra an Israelite," and in the Septuagint "Ithra the Jezreelite." Was he an Israelite or an Ishmaelite? The Talmud presents two opinions to us:

2.27.3.en: The first: R. Samuel bar-Nachmani proclaimed that Jether was an Ishmaelite by birth, and entered the Jewish faith, so he became an Israelite as a proselyte.

2.27.4.en: The second: that Jether the father of Amasa was an Israelite, and was called Jether the Ishmaelite because he lived in the land of Ishmael. This is like Obed-edom, who was called the Gittite (2 Sam 6:11).

2.27.5.en: David Kimchi offers the suggestion that the Israelites in the land of Ishmael used to call Jether the Israelite because of his nationality, while in Israel they used to call him the Ishmaelite because of his residence in the land of Ishmael.

2.28.0.en: 18 And Caleb the son of Hezron begat children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth: her sons are these; Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon. 19 And when Azubah was dead, Caleb took unto him Ephrath, which bare him Hur. 20 And Hur begat Uri, and Uri begat Bezaleel. 21 And afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he married when he was threescore years old; and she bare him Segub. 22 And Segub begat Jair, who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead. 23 And he took Geshur, and Aram, with the towns of Jair, from them, with Kenath, and the towns thereof, even threescore cities. All these belonged to the sons of Machir the father of Gilead. 24 And after that Hezron was dead in Caleb-ephratah, then Abiah Hezron's wife bare him Ashur the father of Tekoa.

2.28.1.en: And Caleb the son of Hezron begat children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth:

2.28.2.en: her sons are these; Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon. [18]

2.28.3.en: Caleb the son of Hezron [18], who is Chelubai in [9], is different from Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite, the famous companion of Joshua the son of Nun, one of the twelve spies whom Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan (Num 13:6; Josh 14:6-7). He was among those close to Hur, the companion of Aaron, and Bezaleel his grandson is one of the skilled craftsmen. Some think that each of them had a daughter named Achsah.

2.28.4.en: Azubah: a Hebrew name meaning "forsaken, abandoned," and she was the wife of Caleb the son of Hezron (1 Chr 2:18-19). Caleb had other women besides her. The sons mentioned here are by her, and not by Jerioth (a Hebrew name meaning "upright"), his concubine.

2.28.5.en: Ardon: a Hebrew name meaning "humpbacked," the name of a son of Caleb the son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 2:18).

2.29.0.en: And when Azubah was dead, Caleb took unto him Ephrath, which bare him Hur. [19]

2.29.1.en: Hur: different from Hur who was also his contemporary, who accompanied Aaron, and the two supported the hands of Moses (Ex 17:10, 12; 24:14).

2.30.0.en: And Hur begat Uri, and Uri begat Bezaleel. [20]

2.30.1.en: Uri: a Hebrew name, a shortening of Uriah, a man of the tribe of Judah, and he is the father of Bezaleel, who was among those who worked in building the tabernacle of the congregation and in inlaying it.

2.30.2.en: Bezaleel: a Hebrew name meaning "in the shadow of God," famous for his skill, and he did the work of the tabernacle of the congregation. The Lord said to Moses: "See, I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah: and I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship" (Ex 31:2-3).

2.31.0.en: And afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he married when he was threescore years old; and she bare him Segub. [21]

2.31.1.en: The daughter of Machir the father of Gilead [21] is Abiah [24]. The Gileadites were the greatest clan of the tribe of Manasseh, and in (Num 32:41) Jair is called the son of Manasseh, that is, he descended from Manasseh through his mother, and from Judah through his father.

2.31.2.en: Segub: a Hebrew name meaning "exalted." Of the offspring of Judah, he is a son of Hezron, whom the daughter of Machir bore, and Segub begat Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.

2.32.0.en: And Segub begat Jair, who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead. [22]

2.32.1.en: Jair: a Hebrew name meaning "he enlightens." He was one of the victors after crossing the Jordan.

2.33.0.en: The twenty-three cities here are in Lejah (Argob), which is in the region east of the Jordan; some think they are a part of the sixty cities mentioned in [23], and others think they are different from the sixty cities.

2.34.0.en: And he took Geshur, and Aram, with the towns of Jair, from them, with Kenath, and the towns thereof, even threescore cities.

2.34.1.en: All these belonged to the sons of Machir the father of Gilead. [23]

2.34.2.en: The sixty cities here perhaps include the twenty-three cities [22], with 27 cities added to them in Kenath (Num 32:42).
